This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 30.5.2023 in connection with Crime No.196/2023 registered at Police Station Myana, District Guna for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 377 of IPC and under Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 3. Applicant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.7.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.24745/2023.

4. Prosecution story, in brief is that on 18.5.2023 in between 12:00 to 13:00 hours applicant forcefully committed carnal intercourse against the order of nature with his own minor daughter/prosecutrix aged about 17 years 07 months who is suffering from intellectual disability.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per prosecution case itself a matrimonial dispute was going on between the applicant and his wife/complainant Seema for last about 5-6 years.

Complainant had made complaint against the applicant before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra,
Ashoknagar wherein her statements were recorded and she specifically stated therein that she along with her children was living separately with the applicant for the last about five years.

She used to give threat to the applicant to implicate in false cases and the applicant has also made written complaint dated 21.6.2022 in this regard to the Superintendent of Police, District Ashoknagar, due to the aforesaid dispute applicant had falsely been implicated in this case.

Complainant herself stated in her FIR that she had seen the applicant committing carnal intercourse against the order of nature with his own minor daughter/prosecutrix aged about 17 years on 18.5.2023 but she has not given any plausible explanation as to why FIR was lodged after about 10 days of the incident.
Prosecutrix is admittedly suffering from intellectual disability, therefore, her statement recorded during investigation should not be relied on without any corroborative evidence.
DNA report is incorrectly issued.
The whole prosecution case is suspicious.
The applicant is in custody since 30.5.2023.
The investigation has been completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Trial will take time to conclude and therefore, in the aforesaid circumstances, applicant is entitled for grant of bail.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the prayer and submit that the applicant is biological father of the prosecutrix who is minor as well as suffering from intellectual disability.
Allegations alleged against the applicant are of heinous in nature, therefore, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

7. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.
8.

Having considered the rival submission, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant, statement of the prosecution witnesses recorded during investigation so also the fact that investigation has been completed and charge sheet has been filed, considering the period of custody of the applicant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence the application is allowed.

9. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
10.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
